hypothesis: Redundant propagation on all positive marks plus full lexicographic row symmetry will let the runtime-enabled CP-SAT formulation reach a feasible scope-111 DTS or a stronger solver status within the same budget.
rationale: The baseline CP-SAT model has a global AllDifferent over 105 derived differences but only weak first-mark row symmetry. Explicitly constraining the 35 positive marks to be all different is logically implied by the difference condition, and full lexicographic row ordering removes remaining row-permutation symmetry without changing the frozen feasible set.
expected_information_gain: Distinguishes weak propagation/symmetry from the underlying model difficulty while holding the solver runtime, seed, worker count, timeout, and mathematical target constant.
method: Run the strengthened exact integer CP-SAT model with the original 42 marks and 105 differences, plus AllDifferent over the 35 positive marks and six pairwise full lexicographic row-order constraints. Use OR-Tools CP-SAT 9.12.4544 from the ignored runtime cache, Python 3.12.10, eight workers, seed 20260826, and independently validate any returned rows.
metric: CP-SAT status, elapsed time, returned rows, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A FEASIBLE or OPTIMAL result accepted by the independent integer validator is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness; UNKNOWN or timeout is solver evidence only and not a mathematical infeasibility result.
kill_condition: Stop after 120 seconds or immediately on a complete solution that passes the independent validator; do not interpret UNKNOWN as infeasibility.
